POST /accounts: Creates a new business on Whop that the signed-in person owns. Use this when someone wants to start a new business on Whop.
GET /accounts/{account_id}/customer_trac: Gets the branding and support contacts shown on a business's customer tracking page. Use this when someone needs to see how a business presents order tracking to its buyers. It returns nothing unless the business has turned customer tracking on.
GET /accounts/{account_id}/fees: Gets a business's fees as one document, including any markups its platform adds. Use this when someone asks what fees a business pays or which fees can be changed.
GET /accounts/{id}: Gets one business by its ID or its public URL name, including its crypto wallet. Use this when someone asks for the details of a specific business.
GET /accounts: Lists the businesses the connected login can act on. Use this when someone names a business and you need its ID, or asks which businesses they manage.
GET /accounts/{account_id}/reserves: Lists what a business's held balance is made of, per currency, with why each part is held and the days it unlocks. Use this when someone asks why part of their balance is held or when it will be released.
GET /accounts/search: Finds businesses by name among the ones the connected login can list. Use this when someone gives a business name and you need to find the matching account.
PATCH /accounts/{id}: Updates a business account's settings. Use this when someone wants to change details of a business they own or of a subaccount they manage.
POST /ad_campaigns/{id}/claim: Assigns an ad campaign and its daily budget to the calling user as its runner. Use this when a user in the advertiser-supplier program wants to take over running a campaign. Only one runner holds a campaign at a time, and the caller must have a verified identity, a phone number and a social account.
POST /ad_campaigns: Creates an ad campaign in draft status for a business. Use this when someone wants to set up a new ad campaign. Nothing runs until the campaign is launched by setting its status to active.
DELETE /ad_campaigns/{id}: Deletes an ad campaign together with its ad groups and ads, and stops their delivery. Use this when someone wants to remove a campaign completely.
POST /ad_campaigns/{id}/duplicate: Makes copies of an ad campaign, which start in duplicating status and become drafts once copying finishes. Use this when someone wants to reuse a campaign's setup. A copy that cannot be completed is deleted.
GET /ad_campaigns/{id}: Gets one ad campaign with its performance stats over a chosen time window. Use this when someone asks how a specific campaign is doing.
GET /ad_campaigns: Lists a business's ad campaigns with stats over a chosen time window. Use this when someone asks which campaigns exist or how they perform.
POST /ad_campaigns/{id}/pause: Pauses an active ad campaign. Use this when someone wants to stop a running campaign for now.
POST /ad_campaigns/{id}/unpause: Resumes a paused ad campaign. Use this when someone wants a paused campaign to run again. The business needs a payment method for ads on file.
PATCH /ad_campaigns/{id}: Updates an ad campaign's settings, or launches a draft campaign by setting its status to active. Use this when someone wants to edit a campaign or start running it. The objective is fixed at creation and cannot be changed.
POST /ad_groups: Creates an ad group, which is a set of ads with shared targeting, inside a campaign. Use this when someone wants to add a new ad group to an existing campaign.
DELETE /ad_groups/{id}: Deletes an ad group and stops its delivery. Use this when someone wants to remove an ad group from a campaign.
POST /ad_groups/{id}/duplicate: Starts copying an ad group and returns the copies in duplicating status. Use this when someone wants to reuse an ad group's setup. A copy that cannot be completed is deleted.
GET /ad_groups/{id}: Gets one ad group with its performance stats over a chosen time window. Use this when someone asks how a specific ad group is doing.
GET /ad_groups: Lists a business's ad groups, newest first. Use this when someone asks which ad groups exist or needs an ad group's ID.
POST /ad_groups/{id}/pause: Pauses delivery of an ad group. Use this when someone wants to stop one ad group without touching the rest of the campaign.
POST /ad_groups/{id}/unpause: Resumes delivery of a paused ad group. Use this when someone wants a paused ad group to run again.
PATCH /ad_groups/{id}: Updates an ad group's editable fields, changing only the fields that are sent. Use this when someone wants to edit an ad group's settings.
POST /ads: Creates an ad inside an ad group, always with active status. Use this when someone wants to add a new ad. The status cannot be set at creation.
DELETE /ads/{id}: Deletes an ad. Use this when someone wants to remove an ad.
POST /ads/{id}/duplicate: Copies an ad into its own ad group or into another one, keeping the source ad's active or paused state. Use this when someone wants to reuse an ad's setup.
GET /ads/{id}: Gets one ad with its performance stats over a chosen time window. Use this when someone asks how a specific ad is doing.
GET /ads: Lists a business's ads with stats over a chosen time window. Use this when someone asks which ads exist or how they perform.
POST /ads/{id}/pause: Pauses an active ad. Use this when someone wants to stop one ad from running. An ad whose campaign is still a draft cannot be paused.
POST /ads/{id}/unpause: Resumes a paused ad. Use this when someone wants a paused ad to run again.
PATCH /ads/{id}: Updates an ad's editable fields. Use this when someone wants to change the content or settings of an ad.
POST /app_builds: Registers a new build file for an app, using a file that has already been uploaded. Use this when a developer wants to add a new build to their app.
GET /app_builds/{id}: Gets the details of one app build. Use this when someone asks about a specific build of an app.
GET /app_builds: Lists an app's builds, newest first, with optional filters for platform, status and creation date. Use this when someone asks which builds an app has.
POST /app_builds/{id}/promote: Promotes a draft or approved app build to production, so it becomes the version served to users. Use this when a developer wants to release a build. Draft builds go through review first.
GET /app_installations/{id}: Gets one app installation with the metadata the app stores on it. Use this when someone asks about a specific install of an app.
GET /app_installations: Lists app installations, newest first. Use this when someone asks which businesses installed an app or which apps are installed on a business. Uninstalled and deleted apps are left out.
GET /apps/categories: Lists the App Store's categories. Use this when someone needs a category ID to set on an app or a category to filter apps by.
POST /apps: Registers a new app on the Whop developer platform. Use this when a developer wants to create an app that offers a custom experience for products.
DELETE /apps/{id}: Deletes an app. Use this when a developer wants to remove an app. The app stops resolving within seconds, a site it serves stops, and a claimed subdomain is held for a month before it can be claimed again.
POST /apps/{id}/deploy: Builds an app's current source and ships it, returning the deployment it started. Use this when a developer wants to publish their latest changes. Only one deployment runs per app at a time.
GET /apps/{id}: Gets an app by its ID, its claimed URL name, its custom hostname or its proxy domain. Use this when someone asks about a specific app. Credential fields stay empty without developer permission on the owning business.
GET /apps: Lists published apps approved for the App Store, and also unpublished apps a business owns when its account is given and the caller has developer access. Use this when someone wants to browse apps or find an app's ID.
POST /audiences/{id}/add_people: Adds people from a new CSV file to an existing uploaded custom audience, using the audience's saved column mapping. Use this when someone wants to grow an audience from a customer list. Processing runs in the background and existing members stay unchanged.
POST /audiences: Creates a custom audience from a customer list or a business's Whop People data, or a lookalike audience that reaches people similar to an existing one. Use this when someone wants a new audience for ad targeting. Processing runs in the background.
DELETE /audiences/{id}: Deletes an audience so it can no longer be used for targeting. Use this when someone wants to remove an audience.
GET /audiences: Lists a business's custom and lookalike audiences. Use this when someone asks which audiences they have or needs an audience's ID.
PATCH /audiences/{id}: Renames an audience, and for an audience built from People filters that keeps itself current, replaces its filters and rebuilds membership right away. Use this when someone wants to rename an audience or change its filters.
POST /channel_members: Adds a member to a direct or support channel. Use this when someone wants to bring another person into a conversation.
DELETE /channel_members/{id}: Removes a member from a channel, or lets you leave the channel yourself. Use this when someone wants to remove a person from a conversation or leave it. Removing someone else needs permission to manage the channel's members.
GET /channel_members/{id}: Gets one channel member and their read position. Use this when someone asks about a specific member of a channel.
GET /channel_members: Lists or finds the people in a channel. Use this when someone asks who is in a conversation.
PATCH /channel_members/{id}: Updates your notification preference for a private or support channel you belong to. Use this when someone wants to change how a conversation notifies them.
POST /channels/{id}/accept: Accepts a direct-message request, or brings back a direct-message channel that was hidden. Use this when someone wants to start chatting with a person who messaged them or wants a hidden conversation back in their inbox.
POST /channels: Creates a private, community or support channel, or returns the existing private or support channel unchanged. Use this when someone wants to start a new conversation or channel.
DELETE /channels/{id}: Deletes a channel. Use this when someone wants to remove a channel. Deleting a community channel also deletes the experience behind it.
GET /channels/{id}: Gets one channel. Use this when someone asks about a specific channel and has its ID.
POST /channels/{id}/hide: Hides a direct-message channel from your inbox. Use this when someone wants to decline a message request or take a direct message out of their inbox. It hides any direct-message channel, including an active conversation, and a hidden channel can be brought back by accepting it.
GET /channels: Lists the channels you can access. Use this when someone asks which conversations they have or needs a channel's ID.
POST /channels/{id}/mark_read: Marks a channel as read and can record which messages were viewed. Use this when someone wants to clear a channel's unread state.
POST /channels/{id}/mark_unread: Marks a channel as unread for the connected user. Use this when someone wants to flag a conversation to come back to. Experience channels are unchanged.
POST /channels/{id}/pin: Pins a private or support channel for yourself, at the end or at a chosen position. Use this when someone wants a conversation to stay at the top. At most 12 channels can be pinned.
POST /channels/{id}/reopen: Reopens a resolved support channel. Use this when a customer's support conversation needs more attention after being resolved.
POST /channels/{id}/resolve: Marks a support channel as resolved. Use this when a customer's support issue has been handled.
POST /channels/{id}/unpin: Removes a channel from your pins and closes the gap in the remaining order. Use this when someone no longer wants a conversation pinned.
PATCH /channels/{id}: Updates a channel, such as its name, icon or notification settings. Use this when someone wants to change a channel. What can be changed depends on the channel type, and one-to-one private and support channels reject icon changes.
POST /checkout_configurations: Creates a checkout link for an existing price or a new one. Use this when someone wants a link to send customers so they can buy. Nobody is charged until a customer checks out.
DELETE /checkout_configurations/{id}: Deletes a checkout configuration so its checkout link can no longer be used. Use this when someone wants to disable a checkout link.
GET /checkout_configurations/{id}: Gets one checkout link and its settings. Use this when someone asks about a specific checkout link.
GET /checkout_configurations: Lists a business's checkout links. Use this when someone asks which checkout links exist or needs a link's ID.
GET /dispute_alerts/{id}: Gets one dispute alert or early fraud warning by its ID. Use this when someone asks about a specific alert.
GET /dispute_alerts: Lists dispute alerts and early fraud warnings across the businesses the caller can read. Use this when someone wants to act on a warning before a chargeback is filed.
GET /disputes/{id}: Gets one chargeback or dispute. Use this when someone asks about a specific dispute and what is needed to respond.
GET /disputes: Lists chargebacks and disputes that customers opened against payments, across the businesses the caller can read. Use this when someone asks which disputes need attention.
POST /disputes/{id}/submit: Sends a dispute's evidence to the payment processor, after checking it against the processor's file limits. Use this when the evidence is ready to be filed. Evidence is locked once filed, and the processor may refuse it, which returns the dispute to needing a response.
GET /disputes/summary: Gets totals for the disputes a list would return, without going through them one by one. Use this when someone wants counts or amounts for their disputes.
PATCH /disputes/{id}: Edits a dispute's evidence while it can still be edited. Use this when someone is preparing a response to a dispute before filing it.
POST /disputes/{id}/upload_evidence: Replaces the full set of evidence documents uploaded on a dispute, beyond the four fixed evidence slots. Use this when someone wants to attach or change supporting documents for a dispute.
POST /domains/{id}/check: Re-checks a domain's DNS, payment and provider state right away, without waiting for its next scheduled check. Use this when someone has changed a domain's setup and wants to see if it works. Get the domain again afterward to see the result.
POST /domains: Adds a domain to a business by buying it through Whop, transferring one in, or connecting one registered elsewhere. Use this when someone wants a domain for their business. A purchase is not charged here: it returns the link to Whop's payment page, where the person pays.
DELETE /domains/{id}: Removes a domain from a business and releases its capabilities in the background. Use this when someone wants to remove a domain. A registered domain cannot be deleted, so its auto-renew is turned off and it is released after it expires.
GET /domains/{id}: Gets a domain by its ID or hostname. Use this when someone asks about a specific domain or whether a hostname is available.
GET /domains: Lists a business's domains, with filters for account, app, status and hostname, or finds domains available to buy when a keyword is given. Use this when someone asks which domains they have or wants domain ideas.
PATCH /domains/{id}: Changes a domain's capabilities or metadata, adding a capability, changing its settings or releasing it. Use this when someone wants to change what a domain does. Capabilities that are left out do not change.
POST /exports: Starts an export of a resource for a business and returns it as pending. Use this when someone wants their data as a downloadable file. The download link appears once the export finishes.
GET /exports/{id}: Gets an export's status and, once it is complete, its download link. Use this when someone asks whether an export is ready.
GET /exports: Lists the exports requested for a business, newest first. Use this when someone asks which exports exist. Only exports the connection is allowed to see are returned.
POST /invoices/{id}/generate_pdf: Generates an invoice as a PDF and returns a short-lived download link. Use this when someone needs a copy of an invoice to download or share. Each call makes a new file and link.
GET /invoices/{id}: Gets one invoice. Use this when someone asks about a specific invoice and has its ID.
GET /invoices: Lists invoices for the businesses the caller can read. Use this when someone asks which invoices exist or are unpaid.
GET /invoices/{id}/sends: Lists the recorded emails sent for an invoice, most recent first, including reminders and payment links. Use this when someone asks whether or when an invoice was emailed. History does not confirm the email reached an inbox.
GET /ledger_accounts/{id}: Gets the details of one ledger account, which holds money for a business or user. Use this when someone asks about a specific ledger account.
GET /financial_reports/breakdown: Breaks one bucket of a financial report, such as payments received or card spend, into the customers, accounts, merchants or campaigns that contributed most, with the rest summed. Use this when someone wants to know what makes up a total.
GET /financial_activity: Lists an account's or user's activity feed, covering every movement of money in or out. Use this when someone asks where money came from or went.
GET /financial_reports: Gets a financial report for a business over a date range, such as balance activity, an income statement or a balance summary. Use this when someone asks about earnings, fees or balance.
GET /members/{id}: Gets one customer by their member ID. Use this when someone asks about a specific customer.
GET /members: Lists a business's customers, meaning everyone who has bought from it. Use this when someone asks who their customers are or needs a member's ID.
GET /members/{id}/logs: Lists activity for a member and all of their memberships that are not drafts, most recent first. Use this when someone asks what a customer has done or what happened to their access.
POST /members/{member_id}/notes: Adds a note to a customer, visible to the business's team. Use this when someone wants to record something about a customer.
GET /members/{member_id}/notes: Lists a customer's notes, newest first, visible to the business's team. Use this when someone asks what has been noted about a customer.
PATCH /members/{id}: Updates a member, such as the customer name the business's invoices show for them, or their email subscription status. Use this when someone wants to correct a customer's name or change whether they get marketing email. It does not change the user's Whop profile.
POST /memberships/{id}/cancel: Cancels a customer's membership, now or at the end of the billing period. Use this when someone wants to end a customer's membership. Buy-now-pay-later and non-trial split-pay memberships cannot be cancelled by the buyer.
GET /memberships/{id}: Gets one membership by its ID or license key. Use this when someone asks about a specific membership.
GET /memberships: Lists the memberships the caller can read with their status, filtered by business, product or user. Use this when someone asks whether a person is still a member or who has access to what.
POST /memberships/{id}/pause: Pauses a customer's recurring payments. Use this when someone wants to stop charging a member for now. They keep access but are not charged until the membership is resumed.
POST /memberships/{id}/resume: Restarts a paused membership's recurring payments. Use this when someone wants to resume billing a member. Billing resumes on the next cycle.
POST /memberships/{id}/resync_access: Re-runs access fulfillment for a membership, recomputing content access and re-checking linked Discord and TradingView access. Use this when a member says they are missing access they paid for. It runs in the background and logs the outcome.
POST /memberships/{id}/transfer: Creates a one-use transfer link for a membership. Use this when someone wants to move a membership to a different Whop account. Opening the link while signed in to another account claims the membership onto it.
POST /partners: Enrolls the calling user in the Whop partner program so their partner businesses become eligible for earnings. Use this when someone wants to become a Whop partner. Enrolling again keeps the original enrollment time.
GET /partners/businesses/{id}/earnings: Lists the earnings Whop pays out for one referred business's activity, most recent first. Use this when a referrer asks what a referred business has earned them.
GET /partners/fee_options: Lists, per income stream, the fee a business the caller refers would be charged, how low the caller may price it, and the commission the caller earns. Use this when someone wants to price a referral deal before the business exists.
GET /partners/businesses/{id}: Gets one referred business and its referral terms. Use this when a referrer asks about a specific business they referred.
GET /partners/leaderboard: Ranks referrers by partner business earnings over a chosen period, all-time by default. Use this when someone asks how referrers rank. Signed-in callers also see their own standing.
GET /partners/businesses: Lists the businesses the connected user referred onto Whop, most recent first. Use this when a referrer asks which businesses they brought in.
GET /partners/{id}: Gets the connected user's partner profile, including enrollment and verification status, certification progress, active referral count and default payout rates. Use this when someone asks about their own partner status. Other users' profiles are not accessible.
GET /payments/{id}/fees: Gets the fee breakdown of one payment, such as Whop's fee, processing and affiliate lines, in the currency each was collected in and the payment's settlement currency. Use this when someone asks where a payment's fees went.
GET /payments/{id}: Gets one payment, including every item bought with its quantity and subtotal. Use this when someone asks about a specific payment. Related records such as the membership or refunds come back as IDs.
GET /payments/{payment_id}/levels_rebate: Gets the part of a business's monthly Whop Levels rebate that a card payment earned, once the month its fee posted in has closed. Use this when someone asks about the rebate on a payment. The rebate itself is paid monthly as one sum.
GET /payments: Lists sales and payments, newest first, with who paid, how much, when and whether each succeeded, failed or was refunded. Use this when someone asks about revenue, a customer's charge or failed payments.
GET /payments/summary: Gets totals for the payments a list would return, such as counts by status, using the same filters. Use this when someone wants totals without going through each payment.
GET /people/{id}: Gets one person for a business, found by person ID, user ID, email address or phone number. Use this when someone asks about a specific visitor or customer.
GET /people: Lists the people of a business, meaning visitors and customers built from pixel, payment and platform activity, with filters and sorting. Use this when someone wants to segment their audience.
GET /permissions: Lists permission actions and whether the connected login is granted each one for a resource. Use this when someone asks whether they are allowed to do something. It describes only the connected login.
GET /product_affiliates: Lists affiliate enrollments for a business's products, newest first, including affiliates with no referrals yet. Use this when someone asks who promotes which products.
POST /products: Creates a new product for a business to sell. Use this when someone wants to add something to sell. Its prices are added afterward as variants.
DELETE /products/{id}: Deletes a product. Use this when someone wants to remove a product. Only products with no memberships, entries, reviews or invoices can be deleted.
GET /products/{id}: Gets one product. Use this when someone asks about a specific product.
GET /products: Lists the products a business sells, or products on the public Whop marketplace when no business is given. Use this when someone asks what they sell or needs a product's ID.
POST /products/{id}/publish: Submits an App Store app's product for review, which moves it to pending review until a Whop reviewer approves it. Use this when a developer wants their app listed. Other products can no longer be listed on the marketplace.
POST /products/{id}/unpublish: Removes a product from the whop.com marketplace and moves it to not available. Use this when someone wants a product off the marketplace.
PATCH /products/{id}: Changes a product's name, description, visibility or other settings. Use this when someone wants to edit a product.
POST /promo_codes/{id}/activate: Turns a promo code back on so customers can use it at checkout. Use this when someone wants to re-enable a deactivated code.
POST /promo_codes: Creates a promo code, which is a discount code, for a business. Use this when someone wants to offer customers a discount.
POST /promo_codes/{id}/deactivate: Turns off a promo code so it can no longer be used at checkout. Use this when someone wants to pause a discount.
DELETE /promo_codes/{id}: Archives a promo code so it cannot be used in future checkouts. Use this when someone wants to retire a discount code.
GET /promo_codes/{id}: Gets one promo code. Use this when someone asks about a specific discount code.
GET /promo_codes: Lists a business's promo codes and discounts. Use this when someone asks which discount codes exist or needs a code's ID.
GET /refunds/{id}: Gets one refund. Use this when someone asks about a specific refund.
GET /refunds: Lists refunds that have been issued, filtered by exactly one of payment, business or user, and optionally by date. Use this when someone asks which refunds were given.
POST /resolution_center_cases/{id}/appea: Appeals a decision, as the customer, on a case that closed in the merchant's favor, which escalates it to Whop for review. Use this when a customer disagrees with a decision. A case can be appealed once, within 7 days of the decision.
POST /resolution_center_cases: Opens a case, as the customer, against one of their own payments, with a reason and a message. Use this when a customer wants to complain about a purchase or request a refund.
POST /resolution_center_cases/{id}/deny: Denies a case, as the merchant, which rejects the claim and closes the case with no refund. Use this when a business disagrees with a customer's complaint.
GET /resolution_center_cases/{id}/events: Lists a case's timeline, newest first. Use this when someone asks what has happened on a case. A merchant sees the full timeline and a customer sees only what is shown to customers.
GET /resolution_center_cases/{id}: Gets one Resolution Center case with its full timeline. Use this when someone asks about a specific complaint or refund request.
GET /resolution_center_cases: Lists buyer complaints and refund requests in the Resolution Center. Use this when someone asks which cases are open. Without a business given, it covers cases opened as a buyer and cases on businesses the user's team manages.
POST /resolution_center_cases/{id}/reply: Replies on a case that is waiting for information, answering Whop's request as the merchant or providing what was asked as the customer. Use this when someone needs to respond to a case.
POST /resolution_center_cases/{id}/reque: Asks the customer for more information on a case, as the merchant. Use this when a business needs more detail before deciding. It is allowed up to 3 times per case before the merchant must accept or deny.
GET /resolution_center_cases/summary: Gets totals for the cases a list would return, using the same filters. Use this when someone wants case counts without going through each one.
POST /resolution_center_cases/{id}/withd: Withdraws a case the user opened as the customer. Use this when a customer wants to cancel their complaint. It works only while the case is still open.
GET /review_reports: Lists the reports filed against customer reviews on the businesses the caller can moderate, newest first. Use this when someone asks whether a review was reported and where the report stands.
GET /reviews/{id}: Gets one published review. Use this when someone asks about a specific review. Unpublished reviews are not found.
GET /reviews: Lists published customer reviews for a product or business. Use this when someone asks what customers are saying.
POST /shipments: Attaches a carrier tracking number to a payment and starts tracking it. Use this when someone has shipped an order and wants to record the tracking number.
GET /shipments/{id}: Gets one shipment by its ID or by the ID of the payment it fulfills. Use this when someone asks where an order is.
GET /shipments: Lists a business's shipments. Use this when someone asks which orders have shipped or need tracking.
POST /shipments/lookup: Finds the delivery for a purchase from a business with customer tracking turned on, using one order or tracking number plus the buyer's receipt email. Use this when a buyer wants to know where their order is. It needs no sign-in and is limited to a small number of attempts per hour.
PATCH /shipments/{id}: Updates a shipment's tracking number and re-tracks it with the carrier. Use this when someone entered the wrong tracking number or the package was sent with a different one.
GET /stats/reports: Lists every report of totals that are not grouped over time, with the breakdowns and columns each accepts. Use this when someone wants to know what a report can return.
GET /stats/time_series/{metric}: Charts a business metric over time for a business or user, as points over a date range. Use this when someone asks about a trend, such as revenue by day.
GET /stats/time_series: Lists the business metrics that can be charted over time, with each one's unit and the properties it can be filtered or broken down by. Use this when someone needs to know which metrics are available.
DELETE /team_members/{id}: Removes a team member from a business, or revokes a pending invite. Use this when someone wants to take away a person's team access. The account owner cannot be removed.
GET /team_members/{id}: Gets one team member or pending invite by ID. Use this when someone asks about a specific team member.
GET /team_members: Lists a business's team members, including pending invites. Use this when someone asks who is on the team and what their roles are.
GET /users/{id}/access/{resource_id}: Checks whether a user has access to a business, product or experience the caller can reach. Use this when someone asks if a person can use or see something.
GET /users/{user_id}/fees: Gets the fees charged when the connected user moves money with their personal balance, such as withdrawals, transfers and bank deposits. Use this when someone asks what it costs to move their own money. Only your own fees can be retrieved.
GET /users/{id}: Gets a user by tag or username, or the signed-in user. Use this when someone asks about a specific user. Private fields such as email and balance are filled in only for the signed-in user.
GET /users: Finds users by name or username, ranked by closeness to the signed-in user, or lists the most recently followed users when no query is given. Use this when someone needs to look up a person.
GET /users/me: Gets the signed-in user, including private fields such as email and balance. Use this when someone asks about their own profile.
GET /users/me/preferences: Gets the signed-in user's settings document. Use this when someone asks about their account preferences.
GET /users/me/preferences/notifications/: Lists the signed-in user's notification levels for each experience. Use this when someone asks how they are notified about specific apps. Experiences with no level set are omitted and default to all.
Lists the signed-in user's notification preferences by topic, along with the platform defaults. Use this when someone asks what topics they get notified about.
PATCH /users/me/preferences/notification: Sets the signed-in user's notification preferences for experiences and topics. Use this when someone wants to change how they are notified. All entries apply together, and if any entry is rejected none are saved.
PATCH /users/{id}: Updates a user's profile, addressed by tag, username or the signed-in user. Use this when someone wants to change profile details. It changes the signed-in user's own global profile.
PATCH /users/me: Updates the signed-in user's global profile, or their profile for one business when a business is given. Use this when someone wants to edit their own profile.
POST /variants: Adds a price to a product, including the amount, one-time or recurring billing, and when it is available to buy. Use this when someone wants to set how a product is priced.
DELETE /variants/{id}: Deletes a variant from a product so it stops selling immediately. Use this when someone wants to remove a price. Existing memberships on it are unaffected.
GET /variants/{id}: Gets one price option of a product. Use this when someone asks about a specific variant.
GET /variants: Lists the prices a product is sold at. Use this when someone asks how a product is priced or needs a variant's ID.
PATCH /variants/{id}: Changes a price's amount, billing interval, visibility, stock or other settings. Use this when someone wants to edit a variant. It changes what customers are charged.
POST /waitlist_entries/{id}/cancel: Withdraws a pending waitlist signup, either the user's own or one submitted for a business they manage. Use this when someone wants to leave a waitlist. It does not cancel an approved membership.
POST /waitlist_entries: Joins a free waitlist variant as the signed-in user, or for a business when given. Use this when someone wants to sign up for a waitlist. Paid variants are rejected, and joining takes no payment method and grants no membership.
POST /waitlist_entries/{id}/deny: Denies a pending waitlist signup. Use this when a seller wants to turn down a person waiting to join.
GET /waitlist_entries/{id}: Gets one waitlist signup, either the user's own or one on an account they can read. Use this when someone asks about a specific signup.
GET /waitlist_entries: Lists the waitlist signups the caller can see, including their own and those to businesses they are authorized on. Use this when someone asks who is waiting to join.
